archetypes.name: robustness
archetypes.rationale: The new write_reviewer_status_tsv is called at 3 separate call sites in execute_round and also from _run_round_body; each call suppresses OSError over a wide scope (mkdir, read_text, realpath, write_text, copyfile) which can silently hide real I/O errors, and repeated calls on the same round may overwrite a previously correct file with stale data.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine every call site of write_reviewer_status_tsv in plan_review_round.py and plan_review.py. For each site, determine whether the surrounding contextlib.suppress(OSError) is scoped tightly enough: does it inadvertently suppress errors from round_dir.mkdir, collector.read_text, or out.write_text in addition to the intended copyfile? Verify that repeated calls to write_reviewer_status_tsv for the same round (e.g., once at the collect-failed terminal and once after _compose_findings_from_collector) cannot produce a stale or incorrect file by overwriting a more-recent write. Check whether the status_by_norm_basename dict in write_reviewer_status_tsv silently drops status information when two different collector REVIEWER_FILE values normalize to the same basename key. In _run_round_body, confirm that the not round_status.is_file() condition (which returns True for broken symlinks) cannot cause write_reviewer_status_tsv to be called on a round where the subprocess already wrote a valid symlink-target file. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: join-logic
archetypes.rationale: The manifest-to-collector join uses a three-tier lookup (exact path, normalized basename, realpath) that can produce false-positive status matches when two manifest slots share the same normalized basename, and the normalized-basename index is built from collector paths only, so a manifest slot whose own output path carries a phase/retry suffix would never match the normalized index.
archetypes.prompt_body: Analyze _normalize_reviewer_output_basename in plan_review_round.py: confirm the while-True loop correctly handles all stacked suffix combinations (e.g., -phase3-retry, -retry-phase2, -phase2-phase3) and does not loop infinitely or strip too aggressively on stems that happen to end with a suffix string as part of their real name. In write_reviewer_status_tsv, the status_by_norm_basename dict is keyed by normalizing the collector's REVIEWER_FILE; the lookup key is _normalize_reviewer_output_basename(output) where output comes from the manifest. If the manifest records a phase-N path as the slot output (rather than the phase-1 baseline path), the lookup would strip the suffix from the manifest side too, potentially matching a different slot's collector record. Determine whether the manifest can legally contain phase-N output paths and whether that creates a false-positive join. Also verify that the os.path.realpath call on reviewer_file (which originates from collector-results.env, an on-disk file written by a subprocess) cannot resolve to a path outside the design tmpdir that then pollutes the status_by_output dict with an unintended entry. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
